title: Telling a story: primero, luego, al final
summary: Link a past narrative together: primero, luego, como, así que, pero, sin embargo, además, al final.
focus: Discourse connectors for sequence, cause, contrast and addition in a past narrative
content:
## Putting events in order

A story needs signposts, words that tell the listener what happened next.

| connector | meaning |
|---|---|
| **primero** | first |
| **luego** / **después** | then, afterwards |
| **más tarde** | later |
| **entonces** | then, at that point |
| **al final** | in the end |

- **Primero preparé un bocadillo; luego cogí la bici y salí de casa.** (First I made a sandwich; then I took the bike and left the house.)
- **Más tarde empezó a llover.** (Later it started to rain.)
- **Entonces le pregunté si quería venir.** (Then I asked her if she wanted to come.)
- **Al final volvimos a casa.** (In the end we went home.)

**Después de** + infinitive or noun gives the order in one clause: **Después de comer, salimos.**

## Because and so: cause and result

| connector | position | example |
|---|---|---|
| **porque** (because) | after the result | **Me quedé en casa porque llovía.** |
| **como** (since, as) | at the start of the sentence | **Como llovía, me quedé en casa.** |
| **por eso** / **así que** (so, that's why) | before the result | **Llovía, así que me quedé en casa.** |

The facts are the same in all three; only the order changes. **Como** must open the sentence; **porque** must not (except when answering **¿por qué?**).

## But, although, however, and also

Contrast:

- **pero** joins two halves: **Tenía mucho trabajo, pero aceptó.** (She had a lot of work, but she accepted.)
- **aunque** (although) introduces the obstacle: **Aunque llovía, nos quedamos en la playa.**
- **sin embargo** (however) opens a new sentence, with a comma: **Empezó a llover. Sin embargo, no nos fuimos.**

Addition:

- **también** (also) sits inside the sentence: **Clara también vino.**
- **además** (besides, what's more) adds a new point: **Además, el agua estaba caliente.**

## A short story

Background in the **imperfect**, events in the **preterite**, connectors in between:

> **Era** sábado por la mañana y **hacía** un sol espléndido. **Como** no **tenía** planes, **decidí** ir a la playa. **Primero preparé** un bocadillo; **luego cogí** la bici y **salí** de casa. Mientras **bajaba** por la avenida, **vi** a mi vecina Clara, que **iba** al mercado. **Entonces** le **pregunté** si **quería** venir conmigo. Ella **tenía** mucho trabajo, **pero aceptó**. **Más tarde**, en la playa, **de repente empezó** a llover. **Sin embargo**, no nos **fuimos**: **además**, el agua **estaba** caliente. **Al final volvimos** a casa cansados pero felices.

Scene-setting (*era, hacía, tenía, iba, estaba*) is imperfect; each thing that happened (*decidí, preparé, vi, pregunté, aceptó, empezó, volvimos*) is preterite. **De repente** (suddenly) almost always announces a preterite.

vocabulary.example: Entonces le pregunté si quería venir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Then I asked him if he wanted to come.
In the end we went back home.

vocabulary.example: Como llovía, me quedé en casa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Since it was raining, I stayed at home.

vocabulary.example: No tenía planes, así que fui a la playa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I had no plans, so I went to the beach.
Although it was raining, we stayed.

vocabulary.example: Empezó a llover. Sin embargo, no nos fuimos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It started to rain. However, we didn't leave.

vocabulary.example: Vi a mi vecina Clara en la calle.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I saw my neighbour Clara in the street.

quiz.prompt: ___ preparé un bocadillo; luego cogí la bici.
quiz.explanation: The first step of a sequence is primero; luego follows it.
hints: Luego comes second, so what comes first?

quiz.prompt: No tenía planes, ___ decidí ir a la playa. (so)
quiz.explanation: A result is introduced by así que (or por eso): 'no tenía planes, así que decidí…'.

quiz.prompt: ___ no tenía planes, decidí ir a la playa.
quiz.explanation: A cause at the start of the sentence is como (since, as). Porque cannot open the sentence here, and por eso would introduce a result.
hints: Since or as, at the beginning, takes como.

quiz.prompt: Empezó a llover. ___, no nos fuimos. (however)
quiz.explanation: Sin embargo opens a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'Sin embargo, no nos fuimos.'
hints: Formal 'however', at the start of a sentence.

quiz.explanation: Work versus accepting is a contrast inside one sentence: pero.
hints: She had work… but she said yes.

quiz.prompt: El agua estaba caliente y, ___, no había mucha gente. (what's more)
quiz.explanation: Además adds a further point: 'y, además, no había mucha gente'.

quiz.prompt: ___ volvimos a casa cansados pero felices.
quiz.explanation: The closing step of a story is al final (in the end).

quiz.prompt: Estaba leyendo tranquilamente y ___ sonó el teléfono. (suddenly)
quiz.explanation: De repente means suddenly and announces an event in the preterite: 'de repente sonó'.

quiz.prompt: ___ llovía, nos quedamos en la playa.
quiz.explanation: Aunque (although) links the obstacle to the main clause in one sentence; sin embargo would need its own sentence.
hints: Although is one word and joins two clauses.

listening.meaning: First I had breakfast and then I went out.

listening.note: De repente announces a sudden event: preterite.

listening.text: Como hacía frío, me quedé en casa.
listening.meaning: Since it was cold, I stayed at home.
listening.note: Como opens the sentence; porque cannot.

listening.text: Al final fuimos al cine con mis vecinos.
listening.meaning: In the end we went to the cinema with my neighbours.

listening.text: Aunque estaba cansada, Marta fue a la fiesta.
listening.meaning: Although she was tired, Marta went to the party.

listening.text: La película era muy larga y, además, bastante aburrida.
listening.meaning: The film was very long and, what's more, quite boring.

listening.text: Tenía sueño, así que me fui a la cama temprano.
listening.meaning: I was sleepy, so I went to bed early.

listening.text: Ayer llegué tarde al trabajo. Sin embargo, nadie me dijo nada.
listening.meaning: Yesterday I arrived late at work. However, nobody said anything to me.
listening.note: Sin embargo opens a new sentence, with a comma.

guide.tip: Tell it like a film. The imperfect is the camera panning over the scene (era, hacía, tenía), and the preterite is each cut (decidí, salí, vi). The connectors are the editing.

conversations.title: A weekend adventure
conversations.scenario: On Monday, Iván asks Nuria about her weekend. She tells the story of a trip that did not go to plan.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Qué tal el fin de semana, Nuria? Tienes cara de cansada.
lines.meaning: How was the weekend, Nuria? You look tired.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Fue una aventura! El sábado quería ir a la montaña, pero llovía mucho.
lines.meaning: It was an adventure! On Saturday I wanted to go to the mountains, but it was raining a lot.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: And what did you do then?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Como no podía salir, primero limpié la casa y luego vi una película.
lines.meaning: Since I couldn't go out, first I cleaned the house and then I watched a film.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: El domingo hacía sol, así que cogí el tren a Segovia. Sin embargo, me dormí y me bajé en otra ciudad.
lines.meaning: On Sunday it was sunny, so I took the train to Segovia. However, I fell asleep and got off in another city.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Después esperé dos horas en la estación. Además, no tenía batería en el móvil.
lines.meaning: Afterwards I waited two hours at the station. What's more, my phone had no battery.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: And did you get to Segovia in the end?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Al final sí, a las cinco. Aunque solo vi el acueducto, fue un día genial.
lines.meaning: In the end yes, at five. Although I only saw the aqueduct, it was a great day.

bites.title: Signpost the order
bites.rule: The order runs primero, luego / después, más tarde, entonces, al final. Give each step one signpost and the listener can follow.
bites.example: Primero preparé un bocadillo; luego salí.
bites.example_meaning: First I made a sandwich; then I went out.

bites.title: Cause and result
bites.rule: porque goes after the result; como opens the sentence; así que / por eso introduce the result. The facts stay the same; only the order changes.
bites.example: Como llovía, me quedé en casa.
bites.example_meaning: Since it was raining, I stayed at home.

bites.title: But and besides
bites.rule: pero joins two halves; aunque introduces the obstacle; sin embargo starts a new sentence with a comma. además adds a point; también sits inside the sentence.
bites.example: Llovía. Sin embargo, no nos fuimos.
bites.example_meaning: It was raining. However, we didn't leave.

bites.title: Scene or action
bites.rule: Imperfect paints the scene (era, hacía, tenía, iba); preterite tells each event (decidí, vi, empezó). De repente announces a preterite.
bites.example: Hacía sol y de repente empezó a llover.
bites.example_meaning: It was sunny and suddenly it started to rain.

sorts.title: What does it do?
sorts.why: Sequencers order events; porque and así que link cause and result; pero and aunque contrast; además and también add.

sorts.title: Scene or event?
sorts.why: Descriptions, weather, age and ongoing states are imperfect; each completed event is preterite.

sorts.title: Where does it go?
sorts.why: Como and sin embargo open a sentence; pero, porque and así que sit between the two halves.

spots.sentence: Porque no tenía planes, decidí ir a la playa.
spots.why: A cause at the start of the sentence is introduced by como.

spots.sentence: Era sábado y de repente sonaba el teléfono.
spots.why: De repente announces a sudden event: preterite.

spots.sentence: Llovía mucho, porque nos quedamos en casa.
spots.why: The rain is the cause and staying in is the result, so you need 'so': así que.
Having work and accepting anyway is a contrast: pero.

spots.sentence: Al final volvimos a casa cansados pero feliz.
spots.why: Adjectives agree with the plural subject: cansados pero felices.

spots.sentence: Primero cogí la bici y después salía de casa.
spots.why: Leaving the house is the next completed event in the sequence: preterite.

builds.text: Primero preparé un bocadillo y luego salí.
builds.meaning: First I made a sandwich and then I went out.

builds.text: Como no tenía planes, fui a la playa.
builds.meaning: Since I had no plans, I went to the beach.

builds.text: Llovía. Sin embargo, no nos fuimos.
